standardSource.playlist: Safety and the Tools of the Woodshop
standardSource.policy: Standard source for every woodshop module - one instructor, one shop, one vocabulary. All six machines in his series (table saw, band saw, miter saw, jointer, planer, router table) plus the drill press are confirmed present at The Box, so the whole playlist maps to real equipment. Outside videos appear only where the series does not reach: emergency response, dust health, laser, 3D printing, resin, vinyl, sewing, plasma.
standardSource.singleSourceRisk: Ask the creator for permission to use as course material and for self-hostable copies. Downloading without permission violates YouTube's terms.

_meta.verification: Every url resolves to a real public YouTube video with the title and channel recorded here, confirmed via YouTube's oEmbed endpoint on 2026-09-06/07. Alpine runtimes were read from the playlist page and are exact; other runtimes could not be retrieved and are null rather than guessed. No video has been watched end to end - staffReviewed is false everywhere.
_meta.linkFallback: Some channels disable third-party embedding. The watch?v= url is the source of truth; the lesson player should fall back to a link-out card if the iframe fails to load.
_meta.certRule: Passing a module quiz records knowledge_passed only. Every machine still requires a staff hands-on checkoff before badge access.

roles.primary: Required viewing before the quiz unlocks.
roles.supporting: Recommended depth, or an alternate explanation of the same material.

_meta.softwarePlacement: Design and control software (Inkscape, CorelDRAW, LightBurn, Tinkercad, PrusaSlicer, Silhouette Studio, VCarve/Mach4) is taught inside the machine module it serves, not as standalone certs - the portal's cert model is per-machine. If members later want software skills without machine access, split these lessons into optional non-cert modules.

attendedOperationPolicy.rule: Confirmed 2026-09-07: on the plasma table a certified member may work alone, but may not leave the machine running. Same rule already applies to the laser.
attendedOperationPolicy.whyItNeedsToBeExplicit: Members will generalise from whichever machine they learned first, and they will generalise wrong. The printers are the exception that creates the confusion: an FDM or resin print is SUPPOSED to run for hours with nobody there, so a member whose first machine was the Prusa arrives at the plasma table with the wrong instinct. Teach the line, not the individual rules.
attendedOperationPolicy.theLine: Machines that cut with heat or a blade must be attended for every second they run. Printers may run unattended. There is no third category.
attendedOperationPolicy.portalSuggestion: Add an attendedOperationRequired boolean to the Machine model. It belongs next to requiredCertificationIds and reservationRecommended, it drives a badge on /reserve and the lobby display's machine tiles, and it gives the reservation rules something to reason about - an unattended-capable machine can be booked overnight, an attended one cannot be booked past closing.

modules.title: Shop Orientation

lessons.title: How we work in this shop
lessons.boxMustCover: Layout of The Box, hours, sign-in, the 'if you didn't turn it on, don't turn it off' rule, cleanup, the 90-day abandoned property policy. Dust: fine airborne wood dust is the hazard (not just visible chips); use dust collection and respirators as posted; fine dust can hang in the air after the shop looks clear — who empties collectors and where respirators live. A 3-minute phone walkthrough of the actual space would outperform any outside video here.

modules.title: Resin Printing (Elegoo Saturn 2 + wash/cure)
modules.splitRationale: Recommended as a SEPARATE cert from FDM rather than the single '3D Printing' cert in the portal spec. Three reasons: the hazard is categorically different (uncured resin is a skin sensitizer that can produce a permanent allergy; IPA is flammable), a member who only wants to print PLA should not have to pass resin questions, and resin access should be gated on a safety lesson that has nothing to do with the Prusa. If you keep one combined cert, at minimum make the resin safety lesson mandatory within it.
modules.summary: Elegoo Saturn 2 (8K) with a wash and cure station. Lowest injury risk on the day, highest chronic risk in the building. Prints run unattended - the exception to the shop's attended-operation rule.

lessons.title: Resin safety and PPE
lessons.boxMustCover: In-house lesson at learn/resin/safety. Nitrile only, eye protection, ventilation, skin-contact response (soap/water never IPA on skin), sensitizer risk, IPA flammability, cure-before-trash, used-IPA container → King County MRW (never down the drain), first session supervised.
lessons.notes: No primary video on purpose — hobbyist resin safety videos are not good enough to gate a cert. Staff-reviewed flag N/A; readiness treats empty primary set as clear for this lesson.

lessons.title: Printing on the Saturn
lessons.boxMustCover: Saturn 2 specifics and Chitubox profiles for the resin The Box stocks. Levelling, exposure settings, the FEP check, and what to do about a failed print stuck to the vat film - that one damages the machine if a member digs at it. Also state explicitly that resin prints MAY run unattended, unlike the laser and plasma table, and what a member must do before walking away (gloves off, lid closed, ventilation left running, name and finish time on the machine).

modules.title: CNC Plasma Table (Avid Pro6060)
modules.priority: HIGHEST - this machine is on the website, is the most hazardous thing in the building, and has no certification defined anywhere in the portal spec.
modules.summary: Avid CNC Pro6060, 5'x5', Mach4 control, VCarve CAD/CAM. UV, metal fume, molten spatter, high voltage and an unattended moving gantry.

lessons.title: Plasma hazards: fume, UV, spatter
lessons.boxMustCover: The Box's extraction setup and how to verify it is running. Required PPE and who else in the room needs eye protection. Where bystanders may stand. Never-cut materials (galvanized/zinc, unknown coatings). Fire watch after cutting.

videos.title: PWTV: Plasma Cutting Fume Venting Overview
videos.notes: Industry association source. Industrial in register, which is appropriate for this machine.

lessons.gapNote: This is the thinnest lesson in the set. A single fume-venting video does not cover UV, arc eye, spatter, PPE or fire watch. Worth sourcing more, or writing it in-house from Miller/Hypertherm safety literature, before this cert goes live.

lessons.title: Running a job in Mach4
lessons.boxMustCover: E-stop location - every member should physically touch it during the checkoff. Setting origin. Workpiece clamping and ground clamp. THE ATTENDANCE RULE: you may cut with nobody else in the building, but you may not walk away from a running cut, not for a phone call and not to check another machine. Cover what to do when something goes wrong with nobody else there: fire watch after the cut ends, when to stop and call, and the fact that a plasma fire can smoulder unseen in the slag tray after the torch is off.

videos.title: First Steps to using Plasma Table with Mach 4
Plasma CNC Workflow - Live Stream with Avid CNC!
videos.notes: The machine manufacturer's own workflow walkthrough. Likely long - a live stream - so pull the relevant section or timestamp it in the lesson.

lessons.title: Designing and toolpathing in VCarve

videos.title: The Most Complete Vectric 101 Tutorial for Beginners (Vcarve, Aspire, Cut2D), CNC Router Project

modules.staffPresenceRule: Confirmed 2026-09-07: certified members may cut with NO staff present, but must STAY WITH THE MACHINE for the whole cut. Solo operation yes, unattended operation no. Because nobody else is in the room, the certification is the only backstop - the checkoff should be a supervised full job start to finish, not a walkthrough of the controls.
